item.title: Joint anatomy
item.description:
1. Start with the real construction

The verification use case is an open wooden frame. A neutral CornerBracket connects a side board to the top or bottom board.

4 brackets One bracket at each side-to-top/bottom connection on the front edge. 8 brackets Repeat exactly the same four connections at the rear edge. Later: 3D corner One true corner component on all eight corners of a box.

Front and rear are positions, not boards. There is no front or rear board in this relationship. They only identify which end of the cabinet depth receives the bracket.

Front view: the brackets are outside the wood frame

Four outside brackets. The opening stays free and no bracket is drawn inside the wood. DXF

Depth view: four becomes eight

The first verification uses the front row only; the eight-bracket case repeats the same four connections at the rear. DXF

The bracket itself knows only its own local geometry. It does not know left/right, top/bottom, front/rear or the dimensions of the cabinet. The assembly chooses those placements.

2. Wat is een joint origin? / What is a joint origin?

Nederlands — eenvoudige uitleg

Een joint origin op een bracket (beugel) is het digitale ankerpunt waarmee je het onderdeel vastzet. Je kunt dit het beste zien als een klein lokaal assenstelsel met een eigen X-, Y- en Z-as.

  • Origin (het nulpunt): het precieze punt op de beugel waar het lokale assenstelsel begint, bijvoorbeeld het midden van een schroefgat.
  • Z-as (de normaal): bepaalt welke kant het bevestigingspunt op wijst.
  • X-as (de draaiing): zodra Z vastligt kan de beugel nog om Z draaien. X legt die klokstand vast.
  • Y-as (automatisch): zodra Z en X bekend zijn volgt de derde loodrechte as automatisch.
origin = waar zit het punt?
Z = welke kant kijkt het punt op?
X = hoe is het rond die richting gedraaid?
Y = volgt automatisch

English — simple explanation

A joint origin on a bracket is the digital attachment point used to connect the part. The easiest way to understand it is as a small local coordinate system with its own X, Y and Z axes.

  • Origin: the exact point where the local coordinate system starts, for example the centre of a screw hole.
  • Z axis (normal): defines which way the attachment point faces.
  • X axis (clocking): once Z is fixed, X fixes the remaining rotation around Z.
  • Y axis (automatic): once Z and X are known, the third perpendicular axis follows automatically.
origin = where is the point?
Z = which way does it face?
X = how is it rotated around that direction?
Y = calculated automatically

SolidCraft mates joint origin B to joint origin A. DXF

Conceptual API object

In a generic API the same local frame can be described explicitly with a point and two directions:

{
 "joint_origin": {
 "name": "beugel_bevestigingspunt_1",
 "description": "Midden van het bovenste schroefgat",
 "origin": {
 "x": 10.0,
 "y": 25.0,
 "z": 0.0
 },
 "axes": {
 "z_direction": [0, 0, 1],
 "x_direction": [1, 0, 0],
 "y_direction": "auto_calculated"
 }
 }
}

origin is the position. z_direction tells which way the local frame faces. x_direction fixes the remaining clocking around Z. Y does not need to be authored separately.

The same idea in Forge

For the six main axis directions, Forge uses readable names instead of requiring the vector every time:

Forge Vector Direction
Anchor.RIGHT (1, 0, 0) +X
Anchor.LEFT (-1, 0, 0) -X
Anchor.BACK (0, 1, 0) +Y
Anchor.FRONT (0, -1, 0) -Y
Anchor.UP (0, 0, 1) +Z
Anchor.DOWN (0, 0, -1) -Z 
AnchorFrame(
 origin=(10, 25, 0),
 z=Anchor.RIGHT,
 x=Anchor.UP,
)

These names are only readable unit vectors. They do not add a second orientation system. Arbitrary XYZ vectors remain valid for genuinely angled frames.

The real SolidCraft relationship remains explicit

Forge still lowers the frame to SolidCraft’s own joint information. The readable names do not change the native data model.

A — frame side edge + on + corner can select real topology. SolidCraft keeps that selection associated with changing geometry. B — bracket side point + z + x explicitly supplies the child joint origin and its orientation.

3. Where does the joint-origin frame come from?

Left: frame topology. Right: explicit child joint origin on the bracket. DXF

Parent A: topology-backed

The frame side can use a real face/edge/corner. For an edge/corner origin SolidCraft derives its frame from the selected geometry and keeps the topology by name, so it can follow dimension changes.

Child B: explicit point frame

The current fixture chooses a point on the bracket and supplies z and x. If a point origin omits x, SolidCraft chooses x from z alone, so a part that was deliberately spun around z can turn back when joined.

Calling B a “local reference” is too vague. On this page we use the precise term child joint origin.

4. Zoom in: what do x and z mean at the four corners?

The current HUB75 model gives us a concrete example. The bracket geometry has its own model axes. The joint origin then defines another local frame on that geometry.

The bracket’s model axes and the current assembly-local joint frames. DXF

Do not mix these two coordinate systems.+X/+Y/+Z describe the bracket model. Lower-case joint x and z describe the frame SolidCraft uses to mate that bracket. For example, joint x = -Z means that the joint-frame x-axis points in the bracket model’s negative-Z direction.

The two points used by the current HUB75 assembly

The reusable CornerBracket does not store these as named anchors. The assembly currently chooses two points on the neutral bracket geometry:

I = (0, 0, 0) # inside corner / component origin
A = (0, 0, -w) # one arm thickness below I
B = (w, 0, 0) # one arm thickness right of I

For the front row, both A and B use the same current child-frame directions:

joint z = +Y = (0, 1, 0) # out through the broad bracket face
joint x = -Z = (0, 0, -1) # down along the bracket profile

For the rear row, the current assembly uses:

joint z = -Y = (0, -1, 0) # opposite broad bracket face
joint x = +X = (1, 0, 0) # right along the bracket profile

Four front corners, one by one

Four enlarged front-corner placements. The parent topology frame rotates around the frame; the current child definition is reused. DXF

Corner Parent anchor Child point Parent z Parent x Current child input
Top left Anchor.FRONT_TOP_LEFT A -Y -Z z=+Y, x=-Z
Top right Anchor.FRONT_TOP_RIGHT B -Y -X z=+Y, x=-Z
Bottom right Anchor.FRONT_BOTTOM_RIGHT A -Y +Z z=+Y, x=-Z
Bottom left Anchor.FRONT_BOTTOM_LEFT B -Y +X z=+Y, x=-Z

Notice what changes: the parent x-axis rotates with the selected corner. The raw child-frame definition for the front row does not change. When SolidCraft solves the joint, the bracket occurrence rotates so its child frame mates with that parent frame.

The rear row is the same idea from the other face

Corner Parent anchor Child point Parent z Parent x Current child input
Top left Anchor.BACK_TOP_LEFT A +Y +X z=-Y, x=+X
Top right Anchor.BACK_TOP_RIGHT B +Y -Z z=-Y, x=+X
Bottom right Anchor.BACK_BOTTOM_RIGHT A +Y -X z=-Y, x=+X
Bottom left Anchor.BACK_BOTTOM_LEFT B +Y +Z z=-Y, x=+X

These values describe the current HUB75 assembly implementation; they are evidence for understanding the native joint frames, not a proposal for the final Forge API.

5. What the current Forge code is doing

The current fixture first defines the child joint origin in Python:

bracket_corner = AnchorFrame(
 origin=(0, 0, 0),
 z=Anchor.FRONT,
 x=Anchor.RIGHT,
)

and then uses it in the assembly:

bracket.copy().attach(
 frame,
 parent=Anchor.FRONT_TOP_LEFT,
 child=bracket_corner,
 angle=0,
)

The low-level vectors are still the real data, but ordinary model code no longer has to spell the six principal directions numerically. The readable constants make the intent visible while keeping the mapping to SolidCraft direct.

6. Requirements for the Forge API

  1. The generated data must map directly to SolidCraft’s own joint-origin information. No second orientation solver in Python.
  2. CornerBracket must remain independent of the cabinet: no left/right, top/bottom, front/rear or cabinet dimensions.
  3. Forge must not guess orientation from a class name or from bracket geometry.
  4. Normal model code should not require raw vectors such as z=(0,-1,0) and x=(1,0,0).
  5. The low-level vector representation may remain available for genuinely low-level use.
  6. The solution is qualified first with four brackets, then eight, then a true 3D corner component.

Chosen API: keep AnchorFrame(origin, z, x), use the cardinal Anchor members as readable direction vectors, and keep arbitrary vectors available for non-axis-aligned frames. Forge does not guess any additional orientation.

7. Verification order

Case What it proves
4 brackets The same neutral bracket works at all four front side-to-top/bottom connections.
8 brackets The same bracket and same child joint-origin definition also work at the rear edge.
Resize Width, height and depth changes are re-solved from native references without rerunning Python.
3D corner Only after the above: one true corner component on all eight box corners.

Native SolidCraft references

  • Command reference — joint.origin / joint.create
  • Components and joints guide

item.title: Verification coverage
item.description:
This page projects the source-owned SCPF coverage declarations onto the current Verification owner graph. Linked owner status comes from the current durable build scope when one is available.

Public Python API exports

API Target Declared current Current owner evidence Cases Notes
Box Visual Visual pass simple-box Native primitive and parameter baseline.
Cylinder Visual Visual pass primitive-csg Native principal-axis Cylinder is qualified with explicit Axis.X in SolidCraft 0.48.1; Axis.Y/Z use the same primitive field.
Cone Integration Integration source-level — Public Cone/frustum semantics, parameter preservation and CSG combinations are covered by the shared geometry contract matrix; the pinned SolidCraft 0.48.1 command snapshot proves the native solid.cone contract. A dedicated visual visual fixture remains separate capability work.
Sphere Visual Visual pass primitive-csg Primitive CSG creation is native-qualified in SolidCraft 0.48.1.
Hole Visual Visual pass, pass hole-family, anchored-holes Simple native Hole.at() is qualified directly by hole-family; anchored-holes separately qualifies face-relative repeated placement.
CounterboreHole Visual Visual pass hole-family Native cylindrical counterbore intent is command-, geometry- and visual-qualified.
CountersinkHole Visual Visual pass hole-family Native conical countersink intent is command-, geometry- and visual-qualified.
ThreadedHole Visual Visual pass hole-family Native M6 tapped-hole metadata and modeled-thread intent are qualified by the Hole-family fixture.
Lip Visual GAP source-level — Plastic feature needs a dedicated native fixture.
SnapFit Visual GAP source-level — Plastic feature needs a dedicated native fixture.
Boss Visual Integration source-level — Boss.attach() retains command-level unit coverage; a dedicated native qualification case is still required.
Rest Visual GAP source-level — Plastic feature needs a dedicated native fixture.
Depth Integration Visual pass anchored-holes THROUGH_ALL is exercised by the native hole fixture.
Rectangle2D Visual Visual pass anchored-holes Rectangle2D is authored inside an explicit Sketch and native-qualified through the rectangle sketch/extrude path.
RoundedRectangle2D Visual Visual pass rounded-rectangle-sketch Explicit named Sketch lowering preserves one solved eight-curve rounded profile with four true arc corners.
SlotCenterToCenter2D Visual Visual pass slot-family Native center-to-center Slot constructor is qualified directly through sketch.slot.center_to_center.
SlotOverall2D Visual Visual pass slot-family Native overall-length Slot constructor is qualified directly through sketch.slot.overall.
SlotCenterPoint2D Visual Visual pass slot-family Native center-point Slot constructor is qualified directly through sketch.slot.center_point.
SlotArcThreePoint2D Visual Visual pass slot-family Native three-point arc Slot constructor is qualified directly through sketch.slot.arc_three_point.
SlotArcCenter2D Visual Visual pass slot-family Native center-arc Slot constructor is qualified directly through sketch.slot.arc_center.
Circle2D Visual Visual pass circle-negative-extrude Circle2D is native- and visual-qualified inside an explicit Sketch scope with negative extrusion.
Polygon2D Visual Visual pass, pass xz-anchor, bracket XZ Polygon2D authored inside explicit Sketch scopes is native-qualified for symmetric and positive extrusion.
Shape Integration Visual pass, pass, pass, pass simple-box, anchored-holes, bracket, sheet-fold Core composition node is exercised by solid and sheet-metal native cases.
Parameter Saved design Saved design pass, pass, pass, pass, pass parameter-scope, parent-derived-child-size, parametric-attach, parametric-offset, parametric-anchor Component-local parameters, inherited bindings and parent-derived child expressions are qualified through saved-design mutation.
Placement Visual Visual pass, pass components, four-corner-l Numeric Placement is native-qualified by components; symbolic parameter-driven Placement and replay-safe occurrence.move lowering are mutation-qualified by four-corner-l.
Edges Visual Visual pass, pass, pass four-corner-l, eight-corner-brackets, eight-flightcase-corners Edges.VERTICAL is native-qualified through rounded reference frames; profile-derived and explicit edge selections still need separate coverage.
Faces Visual Visual pass anchored-holes TOP face placement is qualified; other face selections need capability coverage.
Anchor Visual Visual pass, pass, pass parametric-anchor, corner-anchor, xz-anchor Face and corner selectors are qualified by real native anchor cases; AnchorFrame is tracked separately.
AnchorFrame Visual Integration pass anchor-topology-mutation The public AnchorFrame command path is covered with a real qualification fixture, but arbitrary oriented-frame native/visual coverage is still missing.
AnchorTopology Saved design Saved design pass anchor-topology-mutation Explicit edge/on/corner topology is native-qualified through saved-design parent resize; explicitly rotated occurrences remain unsupported.
Axis Integration Visual pass, pass anchored-holes, primitive-csg Axis values are exercised by native feature patterns and principal-axis Cylinder geometry.
X Integration Unit source-level — Covered as an occurrence-rotation and parent-bound token; dedicated command-contract coverage remains.
Y Integration Unit source-level — Covered as an occurrence-rotation and parent-bound token; dedicated command-contract coverage remains.
Z Integration Unit source-level — Covered as an occurrence-rotation token; dedicated command-contract coverage remains.
CENTER Visual Visual pass, pass anchored-holes, rounded-rectangle-sketch Semantic Sketch profile centre; command-level centering and native centred Rectangle2D/RoundedRectangle2D geometry are qualified.
TOP Integration Integration source-level — Cardinal direction constant; combination semantics are covered by API regressions.
BOTTOM Integration Integration source-level — Cardinal direction constant; combination semantics are covered by API regressions.
LEFT Integration Integration source-level — Cardinal direction constant; combination semantics are covered by API regressions.

FRONT Integration Integration source-level — Cardinal direction constant; combination semantics are covered by API regressions.
BACK Integration Integration source-level — Cardinal direction constant; combination semantics are covered by API regressions.

compile_model Integration Integration pass simple-box Compiler entry point is a command-contract API; simple-box provides a concrete generated-command fixture.
run_script Integration Integration pass simple-box Runner entry point is exercised by the concrete simple-box command fixture and the wider qualification suite.

assembly Visual Visual pass assembly-decorator Imported @assembly subassembly construction is command-, native- and visual-qualified.
ModelParameterWarning Unit Unit source-level — Warning contract belongs to Python-level qualification.
ModelError Unit Unit source-level — Compiler validation/error contract belongs to Python-level qualification.

Capability coverage

Area Capability Target Declared current Current owner evidence Cases Notes
Primitive objects Box Visual Visual pass simple-box Native parameterized box baseline.
Primitive objects Cylinder(axis=Axis.X/Y/Z) Visual Visual pass primitive-csg Principal-axis native cylinder lowering passed native build, measurement and visual qualification.
Primitive objects Sphere Visual Visual pass primitive-csg Sphere passed native build, measurement and visual qualification.
Primitive objects Cone / frustum Integration Integration source-level — Public native solid.cone lowering is covered by the shared primitive matrix and pinned command contract; add a dedicated native visual qualification case for visual.
Primitive objects Torus Visual GAP source-level — Not yet exposed through the public Forge API.
Primitive CSG union / difference / intersection Visual Visual pass primitive-csg All three Boolean operators passed native SolidCraft qualification.
Shape transforms Shape.move(x,y,z) Visual Visual pass primitive-csg Translated primitive passed native SolidCraft qualification.
Shape transforms General arbitrary primitive rotation Visual GAP source-level — Principal Cylinder axes are native; arbitrary primitive rotation remains a separate transform capability.
Profiles with Sketch(...): Circle2D; sketch.extrude() Visual Visual pass circle-negative-extrude Explicit circle Sketch compiles to a native Sketch plus ExtrudeFeature and is measured/visually qualified.
Profiles Sketch.extrude(+d / -d / d, sym=True) Visual Visual pass, pass circle-negative-extrude, bracket Signed distance selects positive/negative extrusion; sym=True selects symmetric extrusion. Native direction and bounds remain qualified.
Features fillet() Visual Visual pass, pass, pass four-corner-l, eight-corner-brackets, eight-flightcase-corners Basic vertical-edge fillet is command-, native- and visual-qualified; richer edge-selection modes remain separate gaps.
Features Shape.rectangular_pattern() Visual Visual pass rectangular-pattern Native SolidCraft rectangular History pattern passed command, build, measured geometry and visual qualification.
Features Sketch.sheet_metal() Visual Visual pass sheet-fold Native base-sheet creation is qualified from flat Sketch through formed body, visual evidence and recovered flat pattern.
Features Shape.fold() Visual Visual pass sheet-fold Native sheet fold is qualified with formed geometry, feature history and flat-pattern bend metadata.
Features chamfer() Visual GAP source-level — Add profile-edge and explicit pick cases.
Features shell() Visual GAP source-level — Add open-face shell measurement.
Features with_material() Geometry Visual pass xz-anchor Material creation/assignment runs natively; add explicit material assertions if needed.
Features directional Hole.at() Visual Visual pass hole-family All four qualified Hole-family features use explicit -Z native direction and pass native geometry checks.
Features CounterboreHole.at() Visual Visual pass hole-family Native counterbore recess is qualified independently from the main bore.
Features CountersinkHole.at() Visual Visual pass hole-family Native 90 degree countersink is qualified with conical geometry evidence.
Features ThreadedHole.at() Visual Visual pass hole-family Native M6 thread metadata and modeled thread geometry are qualified; references independently prove the tap-drill envelope.
Plastic features Lip.at()/attach() Visual GAP source-level — Dedicated native plastic fixture required.
Plastic features SnapFit.at()/attach() Visual GAP source-level — Dedicated native plastic fixture required.
Plastic features Boss.attach() Visual Integration source-level — Command-level coverage remains; add a dedicated native Boss qualification fixture.
Plastic features Boss.at() / directional Boss Visual GAP source-level — Explicit placement/direction variants still need a dedicated native fixture.
Plastic features Rest.at()/attach() Visual GAP source-level — Dedicated native plastic fixture required.
Explicit Sketch Sketch.add(Circle2D)/extrude() Visual Visual pass circle-negative-extrude Named explicit circle sketch persists as its own native Sketch plus ExtrudeFeature and passes visual regression.
Explicit Sketch Sketch.add(RoundedRectangle2D)/extrude() Visual Visual pass rounded-rectangle-sketch Saved native sketch has eight curves, one profile and four cylindrical corner faces after join extrusion.
Explicit Sketch Native Slot family Visual Visual pass slot-family All five SolidCraft Slot construction methods lower one-to-one to their native sketch.slot.* commands and are qualified together in one sketch.
Explicit Sketch Rectangle2D in Sketch / extrude() Visual Visual pass anchored-holes Rectangle2D authored in an explicit Sketch is native-qualified.
Explicit Sketch Sketch.add(..., anchor=CENTER) Visual Visual pass, pass anchored-holes, rounded-rectangle-sketch Dimension-defined profiles are centred semantically; offset is reserved for deliberate local displacement.
Explicit Sketch Text2D in Sketch / extrude() Visual GAP source-level — Text2D explicit-sketch path still needs dedicated native coverage.
Occurrences Placement / absolute at() Visual Geometry pass, pass parametric-move, parametric-placement-pair Replay-bound ordinary occurrence Placement now has dedicated native body-geometry verification; a dedicated visual-regression baseline remains separate.
Occurrences parameter-driven Placement / occurrence.move lowering Saved design Saved design pass, pass, pass parametric-move, parametric-placement-pair, four-corner-l Symbolic Placement lowers through replay-bound occurrence.move values and follows saved-design parameter changes in dedicated and frame cases.
Occurrences copy + Placement rotation Visual Visual pass eight-flightcase-corners Repeated copies with absolute 3D Placement and rotation are native- and visually qualified on all eight case corners.
Occurrences group() Visual Visual pass group-hierarchy Native top/flat BOM inspection proves the named subassembly hierarchy and repeated child occurrences.
Assemblies rigid attach() Visual Visual pass components Native rigid relationship.
Assemblies @assembly imported subassembly Visual Visual pass assembly-decorator An imported @assembly factory returns reusable occurrences that compile and build natively.
Assemblies gap Saved design Visual pass parametric-attach Saved-design mutation qualified.
Assemblies local planar offset=(u,v) Saved design Visual pass parametric-offset Current semantics explicitly local to joint frame.
Assemblies angle Visual Visual pass attach-angle A non-square child is quarter-turned by the native rigid-joint angle and verified by bounds plus visual regression.
Assemblies as_built=True Visual Geometry pass as-built-attach A dedicated native case proves replay-bound as-built relationship lowering and preserved body pose; a visual-regression baseline remains separate.
Assemblies standard face anchors Saved design Visual pass parametric-anchor Parent topology mutation qualified.
Assemblies standard corner anchors Saved design Visual pass, pass corner-anchor, xz-anchor Width/height mutation and mirrored corners qualified.
Assemblies eight profiles as two per vertical side corner Visual Visual pass eight-corner-brackets The 4-profile baseline is duplicated in Z so each rounded vertical side corner has one lower and one upper angle profile.
Assemblies four centred vertical side-corner L-profiles Visual Visual pass four-corner-l One neutral vertical angle profile wraps each rounded side corner and is centred in height through symbolic native joint placement.
Assemblies four-profile placement follows parent width/depth Saved design Saved design pass four-corner-l Saved-design 120x80 -> 160x120 mutation moves all four XY side corners while the fixed-height profiles remain centred vertically.
Assemblies AnchorFrame Visual Integration pass anchor-topology-mutation A real fixture exercises AnchorFrame as the child reference at command-contract level; arbitrary oriented-frame native qualification remains open.
Assemblies AnchorTopology Saved design Saved design pass anchor-topology-mutation A fixed explicit topology pick follows the selected parent corner after native saved-design resize.
Assemblies assembly.with_anchor()/anchor() Saved design Saved design pass assembly-owned-anchor Assembly-owned semantic names lower to ordinary native topology-backed relationships and remain associative after saved-design mutation.
Parameters implicit component parameters and inherited bindings Saved design Saved design pass parameter-scope Native SolidCraft mutation proves local independence, shared bindings and derived expressions.
Parameters child dimensions derived from parent geometry Saved design Saved design pass parent-derived-child-size A reusable child keeps width/depth expressions derived from parent parameters and rebuilds natively after saved-design mutation.
CLI --out command generation Integration Integration pass simple-box The simple-box fixture provides concrete command-generation evidence; the wider CI suite repeats the same path.
CLI native solidcraft-cli run/eval/snapshot Visual Visual pass simple-box Native run/eval/snapshot is exercised by the qualification cases against SolidCraft 0.48.1; simple-box is the concrete baseline link.
CLI live --connect / replay Integration Unit source-level — Transport/argument behavior should be tested separately from headless geometry.
